$comment: The OpenTelemetry GenAI attributes the SDKs put on a span, in one file because three of them
emit spans and a table copied by hand into three languages drifts. AXO-139 is the precedent:
five SDKs kept five different lists of rate-limit scopes and they had diverged, undetectably,
because the list was prose in a doc comment. Each SDK asserts its own map against this file.
Requested by Veritium as VRT-AXO-002, CC Argus, whose argus-obs-semconv suite is the external
verifier. The attribute these replace, gen_ai.system, is deprecated in favour of
Status: the GenAI conventions are still Development, so this file records the version it was
written against. A convention that moves is a reason to re-measure, not to stop following it.
provider_name_note: gen_ai.provider.name has an enumeration (openai, anthropic, aws.bedrock, gcp.gemini, groq,
mistral_ai, cohere, deepseek, perplexity, x_ai, ibm.watsonx.ai, azure.ai.*, gcp.*) and none of
them is this platform. The convention says a well-known value MUST be used where one applies
and a custom value MAY be used otherwise, so this is a custom value and not a gap.
It deliberately does NOT name the engine. Argus's table maps this attribute to llama.cpp /
vllm / ollama, which is right for the gateway's own spans -- the gateway knows which backend
served the request. A client does not: no response header carries the engine (measured over
the whole of ResponseMeta: X-Request-ID, X-Trace-ID, X-Prometheus-Instance,
X-Prometheus-Instance-Id, X-Idempotent-Replay-Of and the six X-RateLimit-* headers). Emitting
a guessed engine would be worse than emitting a true custom value.
server.address goes on the span for exactly this reason: the convention names it as what
identifies the actual system behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

operations.note: NOT `retrieval`. That well-known value is RAG retrieval and carries gen_ai.data_source.id to say which corpus was read; a reranker reads no corpus, it scores documents the caller already has. Claiming it would put this traffic in aggregations about retrieval stores.
The enumeration has no image value. `generate_content` is multimodal content generation in Gemini-shaped APIs, which this is not.
The tei.predict.v1 dialect. No well-known value describes a classifier head.

no_genai_attributes.why: A catalog listing is not an inference operation. It reaches no model, so gen_ai.request.model would be null and gen_ai.operation.name would be a value the convention does not have. These spans carry HTTP attributes only -- which is a change: they used to carry gen_ai.system and a null model, and so appeared in GenAI aggregations as calls that used no tokens.
Same: it reads the token's scopes.

span_name_note: The convention's rule, and Argus confirmed it against their own axis when Prometheus offered to
depart from it for their convenience: `chat qwen3-0.6b`. A span with no model in it -- the
catalog endpoints -- is named for its route instead, since there is nothing to interpolate.
